population: 55 medically inoperable patients with peripheral T1–T2N0M0 NSCLC
harmText: Grade 3 toxicity 27.3%, grade 4 3.6%, grade 5 1.8% in original report.
clinicalInterpretation: SBRT achieved high primary tumour control in medically inoperable peripheral stage I NSCLC; this does not establish equivalence to surgery.
clinicalQuestion: For medically inoperable stage I NSCLC, does SBRT provide durable primary-tumour control?

nnt: ≈7; based on 5-year OS in earlier pooled analysis
benefitText: Earlier 5-year OS was 69% vs 54%; long-term pooled HR 0.78.
harmText: Cisplatin/vinorelbine has substantial hematologic, renal, neurologic and gastrointestinal burden.
clinicalInterpretation: Durable adjuvant benefit is clearest in stage II/node-positive disease; do not generalize the pooled 5-year difference to stage IB.
clinicalQuestion: After complete resection of stage IB–II NSCLC, does cisplatin–vinorelbine improve survival?
refs: Butts CA, et al. J Clin Oncol. 2010.

treatment: 3 pre- and 3 postoperative cycles ECF vs surgery alone
population: 503 resectable gastric, GEJ or lower oesophageal adenocarcinoma
harmText: Only about 42% completed all six planned cycles; perioperative chemotherapy adds hematologic, gastrointestinal, renal and cardiac burden.
clinicalInterpretation: Perioperative chemotherapy improved survival over surgery alone; ECF is historical and later FLOT evidence changed practice.
clinicalQuestion: In resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, does perioperative ECF improve survival?
refs: Cunningham D, et al. N Engl J Med. 2006.

setting: Adult Low-Grade Glioma · Early vs Deferred RT
treatment: Early RT vs observation and RT at progression
population: 314 adults with histologically defined low-grade glioma
nnt: Not appropriate; median PFS difference is not a fixed-time risk difference
benefitText: Median PFS 5.3 vs 3.4 years; median OS 7.4 vs 7.2 years.
harmText: Quality of life was not studied in the trial.
clinicalInterpretation: Early RT delays progression but did not demonstrate an OS advantage over deferred RT.
clinicalQuestion: Does early RT improve outcomes versus RT deferred until progression in low-grade glioma?
refs: van den Bent MJ, et al. Lancet. 2005.

treatment: 54 Gy RT + 6 cycles PCV vs RT alone
nnt: Not appropriate; median OS difference is not a fixed-time risk difference
benefitText: Median OS 13.3 vs 7.8 years; median PFS 10.4 vs 4.0 years.
harmText: PCV adds myelosuppression, infection risk, fatigue and vincristine neuropathy.
clinicalInterpretation: Adding PCV to RT improves long-term survival in high-risk grade 2 glioma; apply with modern molecular diagnosis.
clinicalQuestion: Does adding PCV after RT improve survival in high-risk grade 2 glioma?
refs: Buckner JC, et al. N Engl J Med. 2016.

setting: Resectable Colon Cancer · Laparoscopic vs Open Surgery
nnt: Not applicable; non-inferiority trial, not superiority
ci: Interpret within trial's prespecified non-inferiority analysis
benefitText: 3-year DFS was approximately 74.2% vs 76.2%; the question is non-inferiority, not superiority.
harmText: Laparoscopy can reduce blood loss and accelerate recovery; operative time and conversion risk matter.
clinicalInterpretation: Laparoscopic colectomy can preserve oncological outcomes when performed by trained teams; the numerical difference is not proof of inferiority or benefit.
clinicalQuestion: Is laparoscopic colectomy oncologically non-inferior to open colectomy?

setting: Resected Colorectal Cancer · Predominantly Stage II · Adjuvant Therapy
treatment: Fluorouracil plus folinic acid vs observation
population: 3,239 patients after curative resection; 71% stage II
endpoint: 5-year overall survival benefit (estimated under assumed baseline risk)
nnt: ≈28; based on estimated 3.6-point 5-year survival benefit under trial assumption
benefitText: Estimated absolute 5-year survival benefit was 3.6 percentage points assuming 20% baseline mortality.
harmText: Potential diarrhoea, mucositis, cytopenias and rare severe toxicity; assess DPD deficiency under current practice.
clinicalInterpretation: Average absolute survival gain is small and baseline-risk dependent; stage II decisions should be individualized.
clinicalQuestion: Does adjuvant fluoropyrimidine improve outcomes after curative colorectal resection?

setting: Stage II–III · Preoperative vs Postoperative CRT
population: 823 randomized; 799 eligible patients with stage II–III rectal cancer
harmText: Preoperative CRT had lower toxicity than postoperative CRT in the original report.
clinicalInterpretation: Preoperative CRT reduces local relapse and toxicity without demonstrated OS improvement versus postoperative CRT.
clinicalQuestion: Does preoperative CRT reduce local recurrence versus postoperative CRT in rectal cancer?
refs: Sauer R, et al. J Clin Oncol. 2012.

treatment: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² days 1, 8, 15 q4w for 6 months vs observation
benefitText: 5-year OS 20.7% vs 10.4%; median DFS 13.4 vs 6.7 months.
harmText: Myelosuppression, fatigue, flu-like symptoms and hepatic abnormalities are relevant treatment burdens.
clinicalInterpretation: Adjuvant gemcitabine improves long-term survival over observation but is not the most effective contemporary regimen for every fit patient.
clinicalQuestion: Does adjuvant gemcitabine improve outcomes after pancreatic cancer resection?

treatment: Atezolizumab 1,200 mg + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w vs sorafenib 400 mg twice daily
benefitText: 18-month OS 52% vs 40%; updated median OS 19.2 vs 13.4 months.
nnH: Not quantifiable as an excess harm; rates 43% vs 46%
harmText: Grade 3/4 treatment-related AEs 43% vs 46%; grade 5 events 2% vs <1%. Bevacizumab-related bleeding risk is central.
clinicalInterpretation: Atezolizumab–bevacizumab improved survival over sorafenib in eligible patients; assess varices and portal hypertension before treatment.
clinicalQuestion: Does atezolizumab plus bevacizumab improve outcomes versus sorafenib in untreated unresectable HCC?
refs: Finn RS, et al. N Engl J Med. 2020; updated analysis J Hepatol. 2021.
